thread.title: Morning Movers: Kraft Heinz Climbs, Take-Two Interactive Soars, Shake Shack Slumps

author: Ben Levisohn
title: Morning Movers: Kraft Heinz Climbs, Take-Two Interactive Soars, Shake Shack Slumps
text:
By Ben Levisohn Aug. 3, 2018 9:21 a.m. ET What Now? The Dow Jones Industrial Average was little changed this morning following a mildly disappointing payrolls report . As the U.S. trade deficit increase, China laid out how it would respond to additional U.S. tariffs . Apple (AAPL), which became the first U.S. stock to earn a $1 trillion market valuation , will try to keep climbing. In today's Morning Movers, we...
Illustration: Christina Gottardi •...explain why disappointing payrolls aren't a problem;
•...why trade could be;
•...and review earnings from Kraft Heinz (KHC).
Moving Parts Stocks continue to dip after the release of the U.S. payrolls number. But is it payrolls or something else that's got the market feeling down.
Let's review: S&P 500 futures, which had been up 0.3% earlier this morning, are unchanged at 8:47 a.m. today, while Dow Jones Industrial Average futures have dropped 17 points, or 0.1%. Nasdaq Composite futures, up 0.1%, are clinging to their gains.
The payrolls numbers were about as blah as could be, with the headline number of 157,000 missing forecasts but being offset by revisions to June's data. Wages grew 2.7% year-over-year, and the unemployment rate came in at 3.9%. It was a real yawner, even for people paid to watch the data for a living. "We suspect attention will soon shift back toward the trade war, yuan devaluation, and overseas issues," writes BMO 's Ian Lyngen .
Especially if one considers what happened to the U.S. trade deficit: It rose to $46.3 billion in June , up from $43.2 billion in May, which can't make the Trump administration happy. It's already reported to be considering 25% tariffs on Chinese goods, and now China has said it will respond with tariffs on $60 billion of U.S. goods , with penalties ranging from 5% to 25%.
The trade war is already have an impact on China, which was forced to intervene to slow the decline of its yuan , while the Shanghai Composite fell 1%. Pain may not be building here, but it is overseas. Maybe it forces China to negotiate, as the Trump administration hopes.
But then again, maybe not.
Morning Movers Earnings & News
American International Group (AIG) is down 4% at $52.95 after reporting second-quarter earnings . The insurer earned $1.05 a share, compared with the $1.21 consensus estimate.
Illustration: CBS CEO Les Moonves Getty Images CBS (CBS) has declined 1.4% to $52 after reporting second-quarter earnings. The media firm earned $1.12 a share on revenue of $3.47 billion. Analysts were looking for EPS of $1.11 on revenue of $3.46 billion. Embattled CEO Leslie Moonves took part in the report.
Cerner (CERN) has gained 4.7% to $65.94 after reporting second-quarter earnings . The health-care firm earned 62 cents a share on revenue of $1.37 billion. Analysts were looking for EPS of 60 cents on revenue of $1.33 billion. For the full year, it sees EPS of $2.45 to $2.55, compared with the $2.50 consensus estimate.
Dish Network (DISH) has climbed 5.4% to $31.46 after reporting a profit of 83 cents a share, beating forecasts for 81 cents , on sales of $3.46 billion, topping expectations for $3.44 billion.
GoPro (GPRO) has risen 3.7% to $6.21 after reporting second-quarter earnings . The rugged-camera company lost 15 cents a share on revenue of $282.7 million. Analysts were looking for a loss of 22 cents per share, on revenue of $270.27 million.
Kraft Heinz (KHC) has climbed 6.7% to $63.40 after reporting second-quarter earnings. The packaged-food company earned an adjusted $1 a share, beating forecasts for 92 cents , on sales of $6.69 billion, topping estimates for $6.58 billion. The New York Post reported that Kraft Heinz has been in talks to purchase Campbell Soup (CPB), which has risen 1.4% to $42.30 on the news.
Noble (NE) has dropped 3.9% to $5.62 after reporting second-quarter earnings . The offshore energy firm lost 49 cents a share on revenue of $258.4 million. Analysts were looking for a loss of 47 cents per share on revenue of $256.02 million.
Noble Energy (NBL) has tumbled 7.9% to $33 after reporting a profit of 17 cents a share, below forecasts for 22 cents , on sales of $1.2 billion, topping forecasts for $1.1 billion.
Shake Shack (SHAK) has slumped 4.1% to$61.29 after reporting second-quarter earnings. The restaurant chain earned 29 cents a share on revenue of $116.3 million. Analysts were looking for EPS of 18 cents on revenue of $110.7 million.
Stericycle (SRCL) has tumbled 9.1% to $64.50 after reporting second-quarter earnings . The waste-management firm earned $1.17 a share on revenue of $883.3 million. Analysts were looking for EPS of $1.14 on revenue of $896.6 million. For the full year, it sees EPS of $4.35 to $4.55, compared with the $4.60 consensus estimate.
Tableau Software (DATA) has declined 1% to $109 after reporting second-quarter earnings . The data-visualization-software firm broke even for the quarter, on revenue of $243.6 million. Analysts were looking for an 11 cent per-share loss on revenue of $237.23 million.
Tesaro (TSRO) has tumbled 11% to $31.35 after reporting a loss of $2.59 a share, worse than the $2.41 loss expected by analysts . Sales of $48 million missed forecasts for $53 million.
Take-Two Interactive Software (TTWO) has soared 12% to $127.04 is up after reporting first-quarter earnings . The videogame maker earned 62 cents a share on revenue of $288.33 million. Analysts were looking for EPS of 64 cents on revenue of $259.67 million. For the full year, it sees EPS of $1.45 to $1.70, on revenue of $2.7 billion to $2.8 billion. Consensus calls for EPS of $2.04 on revenue of $2.74 billion. — Teresa Rivas & Ben Levisohn
Upgrades & Downgrades

Nu Skin Enterprises (NUS) has advanced 1.1% t0 $76.76 after getting upgraded to Hold from Sell at Stifel.
Illustration: Rawpixel Regeneron Pharmaceuticals (REGN) has declined 1% to $393 after getting cut to Neutral from Outperform at Baird.
Rowan (RDC) has advanced 1.1% to $13.81 after getting upgraded to Buy from Hold at Societe Generale.
SunRun (RUN) has dropped 3.2% to $14.30 after getting cut to Equal Weight from Overweight at Morgan Stanley.
TripAdvisor (TRIP) has advanced 1.1% to $51.73 after getting upgraded to Hold from Underperform at Needham. — B.L.
